gaps.fact: Mexico's southeastern neighbours, Guatemala and Belize: the Codex places Mexico only against the United States border.

The Court's two categories, hot Mediterranean and semi-desert: the country record names Baja's Mediterranean climate and the Coahuila desert, but the chapter says only too hot on paper and slight rain, and no question of either bank asks the climate.
Soils mixed with a great deal of sand: only the country record teaches the granite and sand of the slopes and the sandy alluvium; no chapter mentions Mexican soil and no question asks it.
Sandy soils keep phylloxera away: nothing in the Codex says it of Mexico; the record's old, dry farmed vines are never tied to sand or to own roots.
Premium wine as the goal, with some new oak: no Mexican line on oak exists anywhere in the Codex; only the record's boutique wave after 2000 hints at the ambition.

Chardonnay as a Mexican white stands only in the country record (a minor grape, the base of Querétaro's sparkling wine); the chapter names the other three, and no question of either bank asks any Mexican white.

Zinfandel stands only in the country record's grapes and Barbera only as a distractor in r-1p9cmqyd, whose explanation says it plays a far smaller part; no question of either bank asks any Mexican red, Nebbiolo included.

What Mexican wine law amounts to (both columns print the same cell): no national appellation system or quality ladder, with Querétaro the one protected wine geographical indication since 2025. The country record teaches it with care; neither chapter mentions Mexican wine law and no question asks it.

The Court's share for the Valle de Guadalupe and Baja California, 90 per cent of Mexican wine: the Codex says only most. Recent Mexican press puts the share between about three quarters and nine tenths, so a card should give the 90 per cent as the Court's figure.

The Valle de Guadalupe's Certified profile: the valleys running southwest to northeast through the mountains, which is how the fog and Pacific breezes get in, the elevation, and the valley as a modern winemaking and tourist destination. No Village chapter and no question of either bank carries any of it; the record has the fog through gaps in the hills and the wine route's restaurants and hotels, and the southwest to northeast run and the elevation are taught nowhere. The Court prints 3704 feet/1129 meters; references usually put the valley floor at a few hundred metres, so the figure should be checked before a card quotes it as the Court's.

Whites from crisp and dry to round and full according to the grape, and reds fruit driven, deeply coloured and high in alcohol because of the warm climate: only the record's grape styles touch it, with no line tying colour and alcohol to the heat; no chapter or question does.

The dates of the Court's history cell: Cortés's planting order of the 1520s (named only in the country record, not the chapter), the prohibition of 1595 and its standing until independence in 1821 (the Codex says only before the century was out and never gives an end), and the modern revival from the 1970s (the record dates the turn to the 1980s and Monte Xanic).

No question of either bank asks Mexican wine history: Casa Madero, Parras and 1597 are asked only in the record's region questions (r-e6gqvpyk, r-37z48t4p), and i-u3c5kcd9 asks the Mission grape as a Californian question.

errors.where: js/data-intro.js, INTRO_QUESTIONS i-jieghr8k (Geography & Maps), stem: "A valley eighty kilometres south of the border with the United States"
errors.claim: The Valle de Guadalupe lies eighty kilometres south of the United States border.
errors.correction: In a straight line it is about fifty kilometres: the valley lies near 32.1 degrees north and the border near Tecate near 32.57, half a degree of latitude, some 52 km. The mexico country record says some fifty kilometres as the crow flies (overview; card 1); eighty is nearer a road distance. The stem should say about fifty kilometres, or by road.
errors.source: The Codex's own mexico record (overview; card 1); the coordinates of the valley and the border at Tecate

courtUpdates.now: On 10 March 2025 the Diario Oficial de la Federación published the declaration protecting Vinos de la Región Vitivinícola de Querétaro as a geographical indication, on an IMPI resolution of 26 February 2025: the first protected wine geographical indication in Mexico, for wine from fresh Vitis vinifera must, used only under IMPI authorisation with Indicación Geográfica Protegida or I.G.P. on the label. Mexico still has no national appellation system or quality ladder, and the second search found no protection for the Valle de Guadalupe or Baja California since 8.2023. The mexico country record already teaches it (ladder; card 6; exam).
courtUpdates.source: Diario Oficial de la Federación, Declaración de Protección de la Indicación Geográfica Vinos de la Región Vitivinícola de Querétaro, 10 March 2025 (dof.gob.mx, nota 5751385)

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 0 and Village 0, since no category of either bank carries Mexico; two Mexican stems sit outside the map (i-jieghr8k in Geography & Maps, i-u3c5kcd9 in United States), and seven region questions in the mexico record (r-e6gqvpyk, r-fhe6651z, r-vpwo61ad, r-yc16flpt, r-37z48t4p, r-1p9cmqyd, r-jrn3t4lg) sit outside both banks. The Introductory column is well served by the Régionale chapter mexico: the 1520s start, the crown's restriction, Casa Madero at Parras in 1597, the Mission grape, Baja and the Valle de Guadalupe, the Pacific fog, slight rain, irrigation and salinity, the blends and eight of the Court's eleven grapes. The Certified column is the weakness: no Village chapter mentions Mexico and no Village question asks it, so sand and phylloxera, new oak, the Valle de Guadalupe profile and the style rest on the country record or on nothing, and an examiner's question on any of them would find the owner unprepared. One error, at medium confidence: the eighty kilometres of i-jieghr8k against the record's fifty. Checked and sound: Cortés's order of 1524, the crown's bar on new planting at the end of the sixteenth century, Casa Madero in 1597, Santo Tomás in 1888, the Molokan settlers, Monte Xanic as the first small estate, thirty-two degrees north, Parras near 1,500 metres and Querétaro near 2,000, and the Querétaro geographical indication. Three notes on the Court's own text, which stands as printed: it gives the planting order to the King of Spain, where the usual account and the Codex give it to Cortés's ordinance of 1524; its 1129 meters for the Valle de Guadalupe is far above the few hundred metres references give the valley floor; and its No laws! is overtaken by the 2025 geographical indication logged above. The Certified outcome promises food pairings with Mexican wine although the pairing row is blank; the Codex pairs no Mexican wine. Two searches spent: the first confirmed the Querétaro declaration in the Diario Oficial of 10 March 2025; the second found no wine geographical indication for the Valle de Guadalupe or Baja California since 8.2023.
